references.text: Abram settled by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron, where he built an altar to the Lord. This shows the connection between Abraham and Mamre/Hebron, the place where Jacob now came to his father Isaac.
Sarah died in Kiriath-Arba, that is, Hebron. The identification of Kiriath-Arba with Hebron confirms the location description in Gen 35:27.
Abraham buried Sarah in the cave at Machpelah, near Mamre, that is, Hebron. This shows the family's deep connection to Mamre/Hebron as both a home and a burial place.
Israel sent Joseph from the valley of Hebron to his brothers in Shechem. This shows that Jacob's family still had their base in Hebron after he came there to his father Isaac.
Isaac lived 180 years, then he died and was gathered to his people. Esau and Jacob buried him. Jacob's arrival to Isaac in Hebron (v.27) is the background for Isaac's death and burial that follows.
The Lord appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre. Mamre was an important place in the history of the patriarchs, and it was here that Jacob came to his father Isaac.
Both verses document the same event (Jacob's settlement in Canaan) and emphasize the continuity of God's promise of the land through generations.
A clear contrast between Jacob's departure (Gen 28) and return (Gen 35), highlighting the complete cycle of God's guidance.
Highlights the continuity of God's promise of the land from Abraham's arrival to Jacob's return.
